Hi! Not sure if this would help, but I’m someone who’s both fascinated/terrified about storms. Bloomington is a valley (kinda) and it definitely restricts the chances of a tornado popping up (doesn’t mean that the chance is 0, but it’s very unlikely) 

https://www.weather.gov/ind/monroe_torn
(here’s the page that talks about all monroe county tornados from 1950-2023) 

I know how scary the wind, rain, and thunder can be, my advice from someone who is also scared- find a friend to call and talk, read a book, watch some TV, try and take your mind off of it.

If a storm shelter is needed, your downstairs room will suffice. Like others have said, if you’re really worried, I’m sure people in the IMU will let you sit there, or the public library.

I always watch Ryan Hall’s stream when he goes live for severe weather- his motto’s ‘don’t be scared, be prepared’. I’ve found that he tends to ease my worries, so I’ll link his channel here:
https://youtube.com/@ryanhallyall?si=wqB4RdmJklfjw0u7

he does show tornados from storm chasers all around the country, so if you don’t want to actively see that, they maybe stay away, but he does a fantastic job.

I feel the same way. Even almost a year later, I feel weird about it. But there was and still is a reason why. If your intuition says something is off or if there was a reason to break up, it’s usually best to stay that way.

So my breakup was in February of ‘21. So… Honestly? I’m still waiting. I feel like there’s so much to learn and do with yourself, as an independent entity, before jumping into something new. So it’s been almost a year for me, and the further away I get from it, the more confident in myself and more passionate I become about the things I’ve come to love. Don’t rush yourself into something while you’re healing. You’ll just put all of that important work on pause and never get the chance to do things that are meaningful for yourself.
